sections.text: ### Domain 1 — Tree Biology (Guides 01–02)

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text: What a tree *is* at the cellular and tissue level.

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
```
TREE CROSS-SECTION (schematic, not to scale):

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
BARK (periderm + phloem):
  +----------------------------------+
  |  OUTER BARK (periderm/cork)      |
  |  INNER BARK (phloem)             |
  +----------------------------------+
    Outer bark: dead tissue; moisture barrier.
    Inner bark: sugars move DOWN from leaves.

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
VASCULAR CAMBIUM:
  +----------------------------------+
  |   (one cell layer thick)         |
  +----------------------------------+
    Meristematic ring, 1 cell thick.
    Adds xylem inward, phloem outward.

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
WOOD (xylem):
  +----------------------------------+
  |  SAPWOOD (functional xylem)      |
  |  (outermost N growth rings)      |
  +----------------------------------+
  |  HEARTWOOD (non-functional)      |
  |  (inner xylem)                   |
  +----------------------------------+
    Sapwood: water + mineral transport upward;
             living ray parenchyma still active.
    Heartwood: dead xylem; extractives deposited;
               denser, often darker, rot-resistant.

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
PITH (dead parenchyma, structural center — first year's growth)
```

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
Key cellular structures:
- **Tracheids** (gymnosperms): long, tapered, imperforate cells — water transport and structural support combined in one cell type
- **Vessel elements** (angiosperms): short, wide, perforated end walls — form vessels (tubes) for rapid water transport; separate fibers handle mechanical load
- **Ray cells**: radial parenchyma oriented perpendicular to grain — lateral transport of nutrients and water storage
- **Resin canals**: epithelial-lined channels in conifers — constitutive and inducible defense

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text: ### Domain 2 — Wood Science (Guide 02)

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text: Anisotropic material with three principal axes:

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
```
  LONGITUDINAL (L)  -- along fiber axis       -- strongest in tension/compression
  RADIAL (R)        -- pith-to-bark direction  -- intermediate
  TANGENTIAL (T)    -- tangent to growth rings -- widest shrinkage, flattest-sawn face

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
Shrinkage order:  L << R < T     (L barely moves; T is ~2× R)
  Strength order:   L >> R >= T
  Modulus order:    EL >> ER > ET
```

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text: ### Domain 3 — Dendrochronology (Guide 03)

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text: Trees as climate archives:

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
```
  EARLYWOOD (wide, thin-walled cells)  <-- formed during rapid spring growth
  LATEWOOD (narrow, thick-walled cells) <-- formed during summer stress / season end

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
One RING = one year (in temperate, seasonal climates — not universal)
  CROSS-DATING = pattern-matching ring-width sequences across specimens
  MASTER CHRONOLOGY = composite record extending thousands of years
  CALIBRATION CURVE (IntCal) = bridges radiocarbon dates to calendar years
```

sections.text: ### Domain 4 — Forest Ecology (Guide 04)

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text: Stand-level and landscape-level dynamics:

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
```
  CANOPY STRATIFICATION (temperate deciduous):
  Canopy layer      15–35 m   -- dominant/codominant crowns intercept 80–90% light
  Sub-canopy        5–15 m    -- shade-tolerant species; suppressed trees
  Shrub layer       1–5 m
  Herb/ground       0–1 m     -- ferns, forbs; ephemeral spring bloomers

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
SUCCESSION SEQUENCE:
  Disturbance --> Pioneer (intolerant) --> Mid-seral --> Late-seral
  Gleasonian: no deterministic climax; species respond individualistically to gradients
```

| Bristlecone pine chronology depth | ~9,000 yr | Longest continuous tree-ring record |

sections.text: ## Decision Cheat Sheet

metadata.title: Dendrology - Tree Biology, Wood, and Forests: The Full Landscape

sections.text:
| If you need to diagnose... | Start With | Key Caveat |
|---|---|---|
| A tree-growth claim | Separate primary growth, vascular cambium, xylem/phloem production, ring formation, and resource allocation. | Diameter growth is cambial tissue production, not simple swelling of the trunk. |
| A wood-behavior problem | Check anatomy, density, moisture content, radial/tangential shrinkage, grain, and species group. | Hardwood/softwood names describe lineage, not mechanical hardness. |
| A dating claim from wood | Look for annual ring clarity, cross-dating reference chronologies, missing/false rings, and provenance. | A matched ring date is not automatically a felling date unless bark/waney edge is present. |
| A forest-regeneration claim | Identify disturbance type, shade tolerance, seed bank, serotiny/sprouting, microsite, and competition. | Fire, gap, flood, and harvest systems select for different regeneration strategies. |
| A tree-identification problem | Start with leaf/needle arrangement, bark, buds, cones/fruit, wood anatomy, and range. | Field ID is probabilistic when hybrids, juveniles, or sterile specimens hide key traits. |
| A carbon/old-growth claim | Separate biomass, soil carbon, permanence, additionality, leakage, structural complexity, and disturbance regime. | Carbon credit value and ecological old-growth status are related but not interchangeable. |
